learningObjective: Identify preconditions under which a learned cost model or tuned schedule from one workload transfers to a new workload.

canonicalClaims.claim: A learned cost model transfers effectively across workloads that share operator class, dtype, and hardware; transfer degrades when any of those axes changes substantially because the model's feature distribution shifts outside its training support.
conditions: The cost model's features encode op class, dtype, and shape but do not symbolically model hardware.
The source and target workloads share the invariant axes.
nonImplications: Does not imply transfer is impossible cross-hardware; multi-hardware training can enable it.
Does not imply transfer replaces from-scratch tuning — it accelerates it within scope.

misconceptions.claim: Transfer tuning works for any pair of workloads on any hardware given enough training data.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Feature-distribution mismatch across hardware or op classes limits transfer even with abundant data.

misconceptions.claim: Transfer requires exact shape identity; even minor differences invalidate the cost model.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The cost model learns from features that generalize within op class; exact shape identity is not required.

misconceptions.claim: GPU hardware features are captured symbolically in the cost model, so transfer across GPUs is free.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The cost model is trained on measured data from a specific GPU; hardware information is implicitly baked in.

misconceptions.claim: Failed transfer on H100 must be due to a driver bug.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The failure is expected and follows from the training distribution — no driver bug is implied.

implementationFacts: MetaSchedule cost models are typically retrained per hardware architecture.
Ansor's XGBoost model uses ~200 features per schedule, most tied to shape and structure.
performanceScenarios: Warm-starting a MetaSchedule search on a new GEMM shape with a cost model trained on similar shapes cuts trial count by 3-5×.
Attempting to reuse a Conv cost model for a Transformer attention kernel provides no benefit.
